seoDescription: Learn to play "Ghost of You" by 5 Seconds of Summer (5SOS) on guitar with this comprehensive lesson. This tutorial breaks down the song for all skill levels, covering both the intricate studio version riff with harmonics and an easier version using simple strummed chords. You'll master the song's structure, including the verse, power chord chorus, bridge, and the guitar solo. With standard tuning and a capo on the 3rd fret, you'll learn the exact chord progressions and picking patterns needed to play along.

summary:
## Song Basics
*   **Tuning**: Standard Tuning (E-A-D-G-B-e)
*   **Capo**: 3rd Fret (All fret numbers are relative to the capo unless specified otherwise).

## Two Versions Taught
This tutorial covers two ways to play the song:
1.  **Studio Version**: Includes the intricate, picked main riff.
2.  **Simplified Version**: Replaces the main riff with an easy, strummed chord progression.

## Main Strumming Pattern
For all strummed sections, the core pattern is **down, down, up, down, up**.

> [!TIP]
> This pattern is used for the second part of the chorus, the bridge, and the entire simplified version. Listen to the track to get the rhythm right!

## Studio Version Breakdown

### Main Verse Riff
This is a challenging four-part picked riff.
*   **Part 1**: 3rd fret (5th string) followed by three open 3rd string plucks.
*   **Part 2**: Slide from 3rd to 10th fret (5th string), followed by a harmonic sequence.
*   **Part 3**: 7th fret (5th string) followed by three open 3rd string plucks.
*   **Part 4**: A chord shape at the 5th/4th frets with an alternating picking pattern.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Harmonics Technique**: For Part 2, lightly rest your ring finger over the metal fret wire of the **12th fret** (relative to the capo, so the 15th fret overall) across the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th strings. Do not press down. This creates a chime-like sound.

### Chorus Progressions
*   **Part 1 (Picked)**: Alternating down-picks on the 5th string and up-picks on the 4th string using power chord shapes.
    *   `10th & 12th frets`
    *   `5th & 7th frets`
    *   `Open A power chord`
    *   `C power chord (3rd & 5th frets)`
*   **Part 2 (Strummed)**: Use the main strumming pattern (`D-DU-DU`).
    *   **Chord Progression**: G → Em → Am → Cadd9

### Bridge
*   **Chord Progression**: Em7 → Cadd9 → G → D
*   **Strumming**: Play the main pattern (`D-DU-DU`) twice for each chord.

### Bridge Solo
*   A simple lead part played high on the neck using the 1st and 2nd strings.
*   **Section 1**: Alternates between the 8th fret (2nd string) and 10th fret (1st string).
*   **Section 2**: A short melodic phrase on the 8th and 7th frets (2nd string) and 7th fret (3rd string).

## Simplified Version (Verse)
To make the song easier, replace the complex main verse riff with this strummed progression. Play the main strumming pattern (`D-DU-DU`) once for each chord.
*   **Easy Verse Progression**: Cadd9 → G → Em7 → D
transcription:
## Introduction and Song Overview

G'day guys, my name's Dave Tran and welcome to another Guitar Zero to Hero song tutorial. And by request today, I'll be teaching you how to play Ghost of You by 5 Seconds of Summer.

Now for the basics of this song, you want to detune your guitar in standard tuning, and you will need a capo on the third fret of the guitar. Now, if you want to master your chords back to front, then be sure to head over to guitarzerotohero.com to pick up my free guitar ebook. Or if you want to take your guitar to the next level, then be sure to check out Guitar Zero to Hero Premium, my complete step-by-step guitar course which teaches you theory, scales, songwriting, finger style lessons that you won't find here on YouTube.

Let's jump straight into the lesson. And in this video, I'm going to teach you two different ways of playing this song. The first way is the studio recorded riff, but it's a little bit harder, so I'll also teach you a simplified version with just some simple strummed chords.

## How to Play the Main Verse Riff

So starting with the main riff that's in the verse. When I take our index finger and put it onto the third fret of the fifth string. Now, this is 3rd fret relative to the capo. We're going to break this main riff up into four sections. So with this first position, you just need to pluck that fifth string and then you need to pluck the open third string three times. Now those three plucks on the open third string should all be up plucks, and the first pluck is a down pluck. So in total for this first position, like that. And I've actually indicated the direction of the picking you should use for the riff up in the tab.

So moving on to our second section of this riff. From our third fret, we're going to slide our index finger up to the tenth fret relative to the capo. Now if you're confused as to where the tenth fret is relative to the capo, it's on the 13th fret overall on the guitar. So, we're going to slide up to that note without your index finger. So you need to play it and then quickly slide up. Otherwise, if you don't like doing that slide or it's too hard, just go straight up to the tenth fret and pluck it like that.

The next four plucks are perhaps the trickiest part of this riff, but they sound really cool. Now we're going to be using some harmonics here, and to play harmonics, basically you take your ring finger and lightly rest it on top of the twelfth fret relative to the capo. So, overall, it's on the 15th fret of the guitar, but relative to the capo, it's the twelfth. So you just need to lightly hover that ring finger over the 15th fret. You need to rest it lightly above the metal strip that bridges the 15th fret and 16th fret. So in between those two frets, right above the middle strip, that's where you need to put your ring finger. And you'll need to cover the fourth, third, and second strings. Again, it's important that you're not pushing your finger down. You literally just rest the finger above the strings, don't apply any pressure, and you'll get that really nice, chimey harmonic sound. In the meantime, you do need to keep your index finger here on that tenth fret of the fifth string. And for our four plucks, we'll go third, second, third, fourth string. And those are all harmonics. So in total for that section. It is important that you keep your index finger up above the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd strings, because if you have your index finger touching those strings whilst you're trying to do a harmonic, you won't get that chime. So that index finger needs to be up and your ring finger hovers above that 12th fret.

So moving on to the third section, and we need to take our middle finger now and go to the 7th fret relative to the capo. And our picking pattern is very similar to our first section. So we're going to down pick on the 5th string and then up pick on the 3rd string three times. And in total... Finally, for the fourth section, you move your middle finger down to the fifth fret and your index finger goes on the fourth fret of the fourth string. For this chord shape, we're plucking the fifth, fourth, third, fourth, and then back to fifth string. So it's just a down-up pattern. And the picking direction is up in the tab as well. So it goes down... and when you put all those four pieces together, this is the main riff. And at a faster speed...

## The Picked Power Chord Chorus

Moving on to the chorus and this is a whole lot easier because we're just using simple power chords here. So for our first position, we go up to the tenth and twelfth fret relative of the capo and that's on the 5th and 4th strings with your index and ring finger. Now, we're just going to be alternating between the fifth string and the fourth string with that down up down up down up. And you're going to play that bar four times. Now an easy way to track where you are is to imagine that every beat is played on this down pick. So one, two, three, and then you'll count four sets of three. One, two, three, one, two, three, one, two, three. Now remember you should alternate between a down pick on the fifth string and an up pick on the 4th string.

And for our next position, we slide the same shape on the same strings down to the 5th and 7th. We're going to play the exact same thing just with this chord shape down. So again, every down pluck you do can be one beat and just count four sets of three beats. And then our third position is just an A power chord. So index finger just goes on the fourth string and you're hitting the open fifth. You play that for the same length. And finally, you finish on a C power-chord. So index finger on the third fret of the 5th, ring finger on the fifth fret of 4th. So really nice and easy, remember to alternate your picking between downs and ups. So the full chorus riff just sounds like this.

## The Strummed Chorus Progression

Now the second part of the chorus, the whole band kicks in. And here we're going to start strumming some chords instead of playing that power chord riff. Our chord shapes are going to be G, and then E minor, and then A minor, and then finally C add nine, which is the same as a G, just your middle and index finger go down one string, and you don't hit the open six of the string.

Now our strumming pattern here is going to be really simple. It's just down, down, up, down, up. And in succession: down, down, up, down, up, down, down, up, down. Now you're going to play each chord shape for four strumming patterns. So the second part of the chorus will sound like this.

## Bridge Chords and Strumming

Next, we'll get to the bridge of the song. And the bridge is really easy again. We have four chord shapes. We're starting with an E minor seven like this. So it's index and middle on the second fret of the fifth and fourth, and ring and pinky on the third fret of the second and first string. And next chord C add nine. Then we have a G, and then finally a D. We're using the same strumming pattern as the second part of the chorus, except each chord is only played for two strumming patterns. So the bridge just sounds like this.

## How to Play the Bridge Solo

And finally, I'm going to teach you the solo that's in the bridge, which is really easy to play. So we're going to start with our index finger here on the 8th fret relative to the capo on the 2nd string, and you'll have your ring finger here ready on the 10th fret relative to the capo of the first string. Now, we're going to hit the 8th fret of the 2nd string three times, and then tenth fret of the first string three times. And in total for the bar. And we're going to play that section through three times.

For our next section, you'll take your middle finger and now put it on the eighth fret of the second string and your index finger here will be ready to bar the seventh fret of the third and second strings. You'll pluck the eighth fret, seventh fret of the second string, and then end on the seventh fret of the third string. And you do that twice. And in total, the solo just sounds like this.

## Simplified Verse Chords (Easy Version)

So that's it for the studio version. Now, if that verse riff was too hard for you to play, here's a simpler way of doing it. So for our simple verse, we have 4 chord shapes here, which is Cadd9, then a G, then an E minor seven, so keep your ring and pinky finger where they are on that G chord and just move your index and middle to the second fret of the fifth and fourth. And then finally, we have a D chord.

Now our strumming pattern is going to be really simple. It's what I taught earlier in the lesson. So it's just down, down, up, down, up. So in succession: down, down, up, down. For this simple verse, you only need to play each chord for one strumming pattern. So the easy verse sounds like this. Now when we get to the chorus and the bridge for this simple version, you can use the exact same strumming pattern and chords that I taught you earlier in this video for the studio version. They're really simple, they're just open chord shapes using that same strumming pattern. So the only thing you'll really avoid in this simple version is this main riff. And you replace it with this.

## Full Song Playthrough

So now I'll be playing through the song in its entirety and I'll have the vocal track on top for some context. So feel free to play this back as many times as you'd like to to practice, play along to it, and see how you go.

## Outro and Final Words

Thanks guys, hope you've enjoyed this video. Be sure to head over to guitarzerotohero.com to pick up my free guitar ebook. Or if you want to take your guitar to the next level then check out Guitar Zero Premium which is my complete step-by-step guitar course. If you've enjoyed this video then hit that like button, hit subscribe, click the little notification bell as well so you don't miss out on my updates. Leave your thoughts, comments, questions, or requests down below and I'll see you guys next time on Guitar Zero to Hero. Cheers.
